entries.answer: A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.
A tissue is a group of similar cells organized to perform a specific function.
An organ is a body structure composed of different tissues that work together to perform specific functions.
The human body is an organized biological system made of cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems.
The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through the circulatory system.
The lungs are organs of the respiratory system where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide is removed.
The brain is the central organ of the nervous system and coordinates many functions including perception, movement, memory, and cognition.
The nervous system is a network of the brain, spinal cord, and nerves that coordinates communication and control throughout the body.
The circulatory system transports blood, oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body.
The respiratory system exchanges gases between the body and the environment, supplying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.
The digestive system breaks food down into substances that can be absorbed and used by the body.
The immune system is a network of cells, tissues, organs, and molecules that helps protect the body from pathogens and abnormal cells.
DNA is the molecule that stores genetic information used for development, function, and reproduction of organisms.
RNA is a nucleic acid involved in processes such as gene expression and protein synthesis.
A gene is a segment of genetic material that contains information contributing to a biological function or product.
A chromosome is a DNA-containing structure that carries genetic information.
A hormone is a chemical messenger produced by cells or glands that regulates functions in other cells or tissues.
Insulin is a hormone produced by pancreatic beta cells that helps regulate blood glucose levels.
Blood is a connective tissue that transports gases, nutrients, hormones, immune cells, and waste products through the body.

aliases: what is a red blood cell
entries.answer: A red blood cell is a blood cell specialized for transporting oxygen, mainly through the protein hemoglobin.

aliases: what is a white blood cell
entries.answer: A white blood cell is an immune-system cell involved in defending the body against pathogens and abnormal cells.
A platelet is a blood component that helps form clots and contributes to stopping bleeding.
Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that binds oxygen and contributes to its transport in blood.
A neuron is a specialized cell that communicates information through electrical and chemical signals.
A synapse is a junction through which a neuron communicates with another cell, commonly using chemical neurotransmitters or electrical signals.
Bacteria are microscopic single-celled organisms. Some are harmless or beneficial, while others can cause infectious disease.
A virus is an infectious biological entity that requires a host cell to reproduce.
An antibody is a protein produced by certain immune cells that specifically binds to an antigen.
An antigen is a molecule or molecular structure that can be recognized by components of the immune system.
A vaccine is a biological preparation designed to stimulate an immune response that can provide protection against a specific infectious agent or disease.
A pathogen is a biological agent capable of causing disease in a host.
Inflammation is a biological response of tissues to harmful stimuli and is part of the body's immune and repair processes.
Metabolism is the collection of chemical reactions that occur in cells to maintain life, obtain energy, and build or break down molecules.
Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions within ranges compatible with normal biological function.
An enzyme is a biological catalyst that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed by the reaction.
A protein is a biological macromolecule made of amino acids that performs structural, catalytic, transport, signaling, and other functions.
An antibiotic is a substance used to inhibit or kill susceptible bacteria. Antibiotics do not directly treat viral infections.
Anatomy is the scientific study of the structure of organisms and their body parts.
Physiology is the scientific study of how living organisms and their parts function.
Epidemiology studies the distribution and determinants of health-related conditions in populations.
